cor-bezout-polynomials.title: Bézout’s Identity for Polynomials
cor-bezout-polynomials.html: Let F be a field and f,g∈F[x]. Then there exist a,b∈F[x] with gcd(f,g)=af+bg.

cor-complex-polynomial-splits.title: Complex Polynomials Split
cor-complex-polynomial-splits.html:
1. Every non-zero p∈C[x] splits over C: if deg⁡p=n and p has leading coefficient a, then p=a(x−z1)(x−z2)⋯(x−zn) for some z1,…,zn∈C. In particular the multiplicities of the roots of p add up to n.
  2. The irreducible polynomials in C[x] are exactly the polynomials of degree 1.

cor-euclid-lemma-products.title: Euclid’s Lemma for Several Factors
cor-euclid-lemma-products.html:
Let F be a field and p∈F[x] irreducible over F.

  1. If q1,…,qk∈F[x] with k≥1 and p∣q1q2⋯qk, then p∣qi for some i.
  2. If q is irreducible over F, p∣q, and p,q are both monic, then p=q.

cor-evaluations-dual-to-lagrange.title: Evaluations Are Dual to the Lagrange Basis
cor-evaluations-dual-to-lagrange.title_html: Evaluations Are Dual to the Lagrange Basis
cor-evaluations-dual-to-lagrange.html: Let c0,…,cn∈F be distinct, with Lagrange basis (ℓ0,…,ℓn). Then (εc0,…,εcn) is the dual basis of (ℓ0,…,ℓn) in F[x]≤n∗. In particular, every linear functional φ on F[x]≤n is a combination of evaluations at the nodes: φ=∑i=0nφ(ℓi)εci.

cor-odd-degree-real-root.title: Odd Degree Forces a Real Root
cor-odd-degree-real-root.title_html: Odd Degree Forces a Real Root
cor-odd-degree-real-root.html: Every f∈R[x] of odd degree has a root in R.

cor-real-factorization.title: Factorization over \nR
cor-real-factorization.title_html: Factorization over R
cor-real-factorization.html: Every non-constant f∈R[x] can be written as f=a(x−c1)⋯(x−cr)q1⋯qs, where a∈R is the leading coefficient of f, c1,…,cr∈R (not necessarily distinct), and q1,…,qs∈R[x] are monic quadratics with no real root. Then r+2s=deg⁡f, and r is the sum of the multiplicities of the real roots of f. The factorization is unique up to the order of the factors.

cor-real-irreducibles.title: Irreducible Real Polynomials
cor-real-irreducibles.html: The irreducible polynomials in R[x] are exactly the polynomials of degree 1, and the polynomials of degree 2 with no real root. In particular, every irreducible polynomial in R[x] has degree 1 or 2.

cor-root-bound-general.title: Distinct Roots Give a Product of Linear Factors
cor-root-bound-general.title_html: Distinct Roots Give a Product of Linear Factors
cor-root-bound-general.html: Let F be a field, f∈F[x], and let c1,…,ck∈F be distinct roots of f, with k≥1. Then (x−c1)(x−c2)⋯(x−ck)∣f. Consequently, if f≠0, then k≤deg⁡f: a non-zero polynomial of degree n has at most n distinct roots in F.

cor-squarefree-gcd-derivative.title: Repeated Factors and \gcd(f, f')
cor-squarefree-gcd-derivative.title_html: Repeated Factors and gcd(f,f′)
cor-squarefree-gcd-derivative.html:
Let F be a field and f∈F[x] non-constant.

  1. (Any field.) If p∈F[x] is irreducible and p2∣f, then p∣gcd(f,f′). Hence, if gcd(f,f′)=1, then no irreducible polynomial divides f twice; in particular f has no multiple root in F.
  2. (Characteristic 0.) If F has characteristic 0 and gcd(f,f′)≠1, then p2∣f for some irreducible p∈F[x].

def-annihilating-polynomial.title: Annihilating Polynomial
def-annihilating-polynomial.html: Let T∈L(V). A polynomial p∈F[x] annihilates T if p(T)=0, the zero operator on V.

def-congruence-polynomials.title: Congruence Modulo a Polynomial
def-congruence-polynomials.html: Let m∈F[x]. Two polynomials f,g∈F[x] are congruent modulo m, written f≡g(modm), if m∣f−g.

def-coprime.title: Coprime Polynomials
def-coprime.html: Let F be a field. Polynomials f,g∈F[x] are coprime (or relatively prime) over F if gcd(f,g)=1.

def-divisibility-polynomials.title: Divisibility, Associates
def-divisibility-polynomials.html:
Let F be a field and f,g∈F[x].

  • We say g divides f over F, and write g∣f, if there exists h∈F[x] with f=gh. Then g is a divisor (or factor) of f, and f is a multiple of g. We write g∤f if g does not divide f.
  • We say f and g are associates if f=cg for some non-zero constant c∈F.

def-formal-derivative.title: Formal Derivative
def-formal-derivative.html: Let F be a field and f=a0+a1x+⋯+anxn∈F[x]. The formal derivative of f is f′=a1+2a2x+3a3x2+⋯+nanxn−1=∑k=1nkakxk−1, where kak is the integer multiple of ak (the sum of k copies of ak). Higher derivatives are defined by f(0)=f and f(k+1)=(f(k))′; we also write f″=f(2).

def-gcd-polynomials.title: Greatest Common Divisor
def-gcd-polynomials.html: Let F be a field and f,g∈F[x]. If f and g are not both zero, the greatest common divisor gcd(f,g) is the unique monic polynomial d∈F[x] with ⟨f,g⟩=⟨d⟩. We set gcd(0,0)=0.

def-ideal-polynomials.title: Ideal of F\lbrack x\rbrack
def-ideal-polynomials.title_html: Ideal of F[x]
def-ideal-polynomials.html:
Let F be a field. A subset I⊆F[x] is an ideal of F[x] if

  1. I is non-empty;
  2. f+g∈I for all f,g∈I;
  3. hf∈I for all f∈I and every h∈F[x].

For f1,…,fk∈F[x], write ⟨f1,…,fk⟩:={a1f1+⋯+akfk:a1,…,ak∈F[x]}. In particular ⟨p⟩={hp:h∈F[x]} is the set of all multiples of p.

def-irreducible-polynomial.title: Irreducible Polynomial
def-irreducible-polynomial.html:
Let F be a field. A polynomial p∈F[x] is irreducible over F if

  1. p is non-constant, that is, deg⁡p≥1; and
  2. whenever p=gh with g,h∈F[x], one of g,h is a constant.

A non-constant polynomial that is not irreducible is reducible over F.

def-lagrange-basis.title: Lagrange Basis
def-lagrange-basis.html: Let n∈N, and let c0,c1,…,cn∈F be distinct. For i=0,…,n, the i-th Lagrange polynomial for these nodes is ℓi(x):=∏j=0j≠inx−cjci−cj∈F[x]. The list (ℓ0,…,ℓn) is the Lagrange basis for the nodes c0,…,cn.

def-lcm-polynomials.title: Least Common Multiple
def-lcm-polynomials.html: Let F be a field and f,g∈F[x]. The least common multiple lcm(f,g) is the monic generator of the ideal ⟨f⟩∩⟨g⟩ if this ideal is non-zero, and 0 otherwise.

def-polynomial-splits.title: Splitting into Linear Factors
def-polynomial-splits.html: Let F be a field. A non-zero f∈F[x] of degree n splits over F if there are a∈F and a1,…,an∈F, not necessarily distinct, with f=a(x−a1)(x−a2)⋯(x−an).

def-root-multiplicity.title: Multiplicity of a Root
def-root-multiplicity.html:
Let F be a field, f∈F[x] non-zero and c∈F. The multiplicity of c as a root of f, written multc(f), is the largest m∈N such that (x−c)m∣f.

The root c is simple if multc(f)=1, and multiple (or repeated) if multc(f)≥2.

exm-annihilating-polynomial-3x3.title: Finding an Annihilating Polynomial
exm-annihilating-polynomial-3x3.html: Find a non-zero polynomial of least possible degree that annihilates B=(211010001)∈M3(Q).

exm-crt-polynomials.title: A Linear and a Quadratic Modulus
exm-crt-polynomials.title_html: A Linear and a Quadratic Modulus
exm-crt-polynomials.html: Find the polynomial f∈Q[x] of degree less than 3 with f≡1(modx−2),f≡2x−1(modx2+1).

exm-cubic-irreducible-over-q.title: A Cubic That Is Irreducible Over \nQ
exm-cubic-irreducible-over-q.title_html: A Cubic That Is Irreducible Over Q
exm-cubic-irreducible-over-q.html: Decide whether f=2x3−3x2+4x−1 is irreducible over Q.

exm-dalembert-step.title: One Step Downhill
exm-dalembert-step.html: Let p=x3+x2+1∈C[x] and z0=0. Follow the proof of @lem-dalembert to find z with |p(z)|<|p(0)|.

exm-eisenstein.title: Irreducible Polynomials of Every Degree Over \nQ
exm-eisenstein.title_html: Irreducible Polynomials of Every Degree Over Q
exm-eisenstein.html: 1. Show that xn−2 is irreducible over Q for every n≥1. (b) Show that x4+10x+5 is irreducible over Q.

exm-euclid-polynomials.title: The Euclidean Algorithm with Back-Substitution
exm-euclid-polynomials.html: In Q[x], let f=x4−x3−3x2+x+2 and g=x3−2x−1. Find gcd(f,g) and polynomials a,b with gcd(f,g)=af+bg.

exm-factor-x4-minus-1.title: Factoring x^4 - 1 Over Six Fields
exm-factor-x4-minus-1.title_html: Factoring x4−1 Over Six Fields
exm-factor-x4-minus-1.html: Factor x4−1 into a constant times monic irreducibles over Q, R, C, F2, F3, and, for contrast, F5.

exm-factor-x4-plus-1.title: Factoring x^4 + 1 over \nC and over \nR
exm-factor-x4-plus-1.title_html: Factoring x4+1 over C and over R
exm-factor-x4-plus-1.html: Factor f=x4+1 into irreducible polynomials in C[x] and in R[x].

exm-gcd-first.title: First Greatest Common Divisors
exm-gcd-first.html:
1. Let f≠0 have leading coefficient a. Find gcd(f,0) and gcd(f,c) for a non-zero constant c.
  2. Find gcd(x2−1,x2+x−2) in Q[x].
  3. Find gcd(x2+1,x+1) in Q[x] and in F2[x].

exm-gcd-with-derivative.title: Detecting a Repeated Root with a gcd
exm-gcd-with-derivative.title_html: Detecting a Repeated Root with a gcd
exm-gcd-with-derivative.html: Decide whether f=x4−2x3+2x−1∈Q[x] has a repeated irreducible factor, using only gcd(f,f′). Does f have a multiple root in C?

exm-hermite-via-crt.title: Values and Slopes by CRT
exm-hermite-via-crt.html:
1. Let c,a,b∈F and f∈F[x]. Show that f≡a+b(x−c)(mod(x−c)2) if and only if f(c)=a and f′(c)=b.
  2. Find the p∈Q[x]≤3 with p(0)=2, p′(0)=−1, p(1)=1 and p′(1)=3.

exm-ideals-polynomials.title: First Ideals
exm-ideals-polynomials.html:
Check each of the following against @def-ideal-polynomials.

  1. {0} and F[x]; and any ideal containing a non-zero constant.
  2. Ic={f∈F[x]:f(c)=0} for a fixed c∈F.
  3. For A=(0100)∈M2(F), the set {p∈F[x]:p(A)=0}.

exm-irreducible-polynomials.title: First Irreducible and Reducible Polynomials
exm-irreducible-polynomials.html:
1. Show that every polynomial of degree 1 is irreducible over every field.
  2. Show that the constants 0 and 2 are not irreducible over Q.
  3. Show that x2+x is reducible over every field, and that x3 is reducible over every field.

exm-lagrange-cubic.title: The Chapter 2 Cubic by Lagrange’s Formula
exm-lagrange-cubic.title_html: The Chapter 2 Cubic by Lagrange’s Formula
exm-lagrange-cubic.html: Use @thm-lagrange-interpolation to find the p∈Q[x]≤3 with p(−1)=2, p(0)=1, p(1)=2 and p(2)=11, and compare with @exm-interpolation-cubic.

exm-long-division.title: Long Division with a Non-Monic Divisor
exm-long-division.title_html: Long Division with a Non-Monic Divisor
exm-long-division.html: In Q[x], divide f=2x4−3x3+x2+4x−1 by g=2x2−x+3 with remainder.

exm-multiplicity-by-division.title: Finding a Multiplicity by Repeated Division
exm-multiplicity-by-division.title_html: Finding a Multiplicity by Repeated Division
exm-multiplicity-by-division.html: Let f=x4−2x3+2x−1∈Q[x]. Find the multiplicity of 1 and of −1 as roots of f.

exm-polynomial-of-2x2.title: Two Ways to Evaluate
exm-polynomial-of-2x2.html: Let A=(31−11)∈M2(Q). Compute p(A) for p=x2−4x+4 and q=x2−3x, once by expanding and once by factoring.

exm-quadrature-weights.title: Integrals and Slopes from Values
exm-quadrature-weights.html:
1. Find w0,w1,w2∈R such that ∫01p(t)dt=w0p(0)+w1p(12)+w2p(1) for every p∈R[x]≤2.
  2. Express p↦p′(0) on R[x]≤2 as a combination of ε−1,ε0,ε1.

exm-remainder-theorem.title: Remainders Without Dividing
exm-remainder-theorem.html: 1. Find the remainder of f=x5−3x3+2x+7 on division by x−2 in Q[x]. (b) Show that x+1∤x2+1 in Q[x], but x+1∣x2+1 in F2[x]. (c) Find the remainder of x5 on division by x2−x in Q[x], again without long division.

exm-splitting-3x3.title: A Splitting with a Repeated Factor
exm-splitting-3x3.title_html: A Splitting with a Repeated Factor
exm-splitting-3x3.html: Let A=(01−1001001)∈M3(Q). Verify that A2(A−I3)=0, and use @thm-kernel-splitting with p=x2, q=x−1 to split Q3, giving both projections as polynomials in A.

exm-splitting-involution.title: Recovering the Involution Decomposition
exm-splitting-involution.html: Let F have characteristic not 2, and let T∈L(V) with T2=idV. Apply @thm-kernel-splitting with p=x−1 and q=x+1, and compare with @thm-involution-decomposition. What goes wrong in characteristic 2?

exm-splitting-projection.title: Recovering Projections and Direct Sums
exm-splitting-projection.html: Let P∈L(V) be a projection. Apply @thm-kernel-splitting with p=x and q=x−1, and compare with @thm-projection-direct-sum (a).

exm-taylor-expansion.title: Re-centering a Cubic
exm-taylor-expansion.html: Expand f=x3−2x+5∈Q[x] in powers of x−1.

exr-division-a1.title: A1
exr-division-a1.html:
1. State the theorem on division with remainder in F[x], including every hypothesis.
  2. Determine whether the following statement is true: “for every field F and all f,g∈F[x], if f∣g and g∣f, then f=g.” Justify your answer. Does your answer change if F=F2?
  3. Let c∈F be non-zero. What are the quotient and the remainder of f on division by the constant polynomial c?
  4. Name the method for finding the remainder of f on division by x−c without dividing.
  5. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if F is a field and p∈F[x] satisfies p(c)=0 for every c∈F, then p=0.” Justify your answer.

exr-division-b1.title: B1: Dividing Over Two Fields
exr-division-b1.html:
1. In Q[x], divide f=x4−3x3+2x−5 by g=3x2−1 with remainder.
  2. In F5[x], divide f=x4+2x3+3x+1 by g=2x2+3 with remainder. Hence decide whether g∣f in F5[x].

Hint for (b): first find the inverse of 2 in F5.

exr-division-b2.title: B2: A Factor of x^n - c^n
exr-division-b2.title_html: B2: A Factor of xn−cn
exr-division-b2.html: Let F be a field, c∈F and n≥1. Prove that x−c∣xn−cn in F[x], and verify that the quotient is xn−1+cxn−2+⋯+cn−2x+cn−1.

exr-division-b3.title: B3: A Remainder Without Long Division
exr-division-b3.title_html: B3: A Remainder Without Long Division
exr-division-b3.html:
1. In Q[x], find the remainder of x100 on division by x2−1 without long division.
  2. Show that the answer to (a) is the remainder of x100 on division by x2−1 over every field F, including F2. Explain why the method of (a) alone does not settle the case F=F2.

Hint for (a): part (c) of @exm-remainder-theorem. Hint for (b): imitate the identity of B2.

exr-division-c1.title: C1: Division by a Monic Polynomial Over \nZ
exr-division-c1.title_html: C1: Division by a Monic Polynomial Over Z
exr-division-c1.html:
As in the warning after @thm-polynomial-division, Z[x] denotes the set of polynomials in Q[x] all of whose coefficients are integers. It is closed under addition and multiplication.

  1. Let f,g∈Z[x] with g monic. Prove that there exist q,r∈Z[x] with f=qg+r and deg⁡r<deg⁡g.
  2. Prove that q and r in (a) are unique, even among q,r∈Q[x].
  3. Does (a) remain true if the leading coefficient of g is −1 instead of 1? Justify your answer.

Hint for (a): find the one step in the proof of @thm-polynomial-division that leaves Z[x].

exr-division-c2.title: C2: Remainders on Division by a Quadratic
exr-division-c2.title_html: C2: Remainders on Division by a Quadratic
exr-division-c2.html:
Let F be a field, f∈F[x] and a,b∈F.

  1. Suppose a≠b. Prove that the remainder of f on division by (x−a)(x−b) is r=f(a)x−ba−b+f(b)x−ab−a, where x−ba−b means (a−b)−1(x−b).
  2. Now let a=b. Write f=(x−a)h+f(a) by @thm-remainder-theorem. Prove that the remainder of f on division by (x−a)2 is h(a)(x−a)+f(a).
  3. Hence find the remainder of x100 on division by x2−3x+2 in Q[x].

exr-division-c3.title: C3: Equal Functions Over \nF_p
exr-division-c3.title_html: C3: Equal Functions Over Fp
exr-division-c3.html:
Let p be a prime and f,g∈Fp[x].

  1. Prove that f(c)=g(c) for every c∈Fp if and only if xp−x∣f−g in Fp[x].
  2. Deduce that f and its remainder on division by xp−x define the same function Fp→Fp. Use this to find a polynomial of degree less than 5 that defines the same function on F5 as x7+x.

Hint for (a): @exr-polynomials-c2 and @cor-root-bound-general.

exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-a1.title: A1
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-a1.html:
1. State the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, and list the two facts from analysis used in its proof in this section.
  2. True or false: every polynomial in R[x] of degree 4 has a real root. Justify your answer.
  3. True or false: if f∈R[x] has 2+i as a root of multiplicity 3, then deg⁡f≥6. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: every polynomial in R[x] of degree 5 has a real root. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: every irreducible polynomial in F2[x] has degree at most 2. Justify your answer.
  6. In the proof of d’Alembert’s lemma (@lem-dalembert), which property of C is used that R lacks?

exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b1.title: B1: x^4 + 4
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b1.title_html: B1: x4+4
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b1.html: Find all complex roots of x4+4, and factor it into irreducible polynomials in C[x] and in R[x].

exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b2.title: B2: x^6 + 1
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b2.title_html: B2: x6+1
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b2.html: Find the factorization of x6+1 into irreducible polynomials in R[x].

exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b3.title: B3: Real cubics
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b3.html:
Let f∈R[x] have degree 3, and suppose the multiplicities of the real roots of f add up to 1.

  1. Prove that f=a(x−c)(x−z)(x−z―) for some a,c∈R and some z∈C∖R, and that z and z― are simple roots.
  2. Show that the hypothesis cannot be weakened to “f has exactly one real root” by considering (x−1)3.

exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b4.title: B4: Running the proof on an example
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b4.title_html: B4: Running the proof on an example
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-b4.html:
Let p=x4−x2+2∈C[x].

  1. Compute the radius R of @lem-polynomial-growth for p.
  2. Follow the proof of @lem-dalembert at z0=0: find k, B, u and t, and verify that |p(tu)|<|p(0)|.
  3. Compute p(i/2), and explain why the direction i does not work here, although it did in @exm-dalembert-step.

exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-c1.title: C1: Fields where the theorem fails
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-c1.title_html: C1: Fields where the theorem fails
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-c1.html:
Call a field F algebraically closed if every non-constant polynomial in F[x] has a root in F.

  1. Let p be a prime. Show that xp−x+1 has no root in Fp. More generally, show that no finite field is algebraically closed.
  2. Give explicit witnesses that R and Q are not algebraically closed.
  3. For your witness over R, explain which step of the proof of the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra (@thm-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra) breaks.
  4. For f=x2−2 over Q, prove that r↦|f(r)| has no minimum on Q. Which step of the proof breaks now?

Hint for (d): if r0 were a minimum point with r02>25, compare r0 with r1=r02+22r0.

exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-c2.title: C2: Sums of two squares
exr-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-c2.html:
Let f∈R[x] be monic with no real root.

  1. Prove that deg⁡f is even and that f(c)>0 for every c∈R.
  2. Prove that f=g2+h2 for some g,h∈R[x].

Hint for (b): each irreducible factor of f is (x−z)(x−z―). Collect one root from each pair into a complex polynomial G, and split G into real and imaginary parts.

exr-ideals-and-gcd-a1.title: A1
exr-ideals-and-gcd-a1.html:
1. Define an ideal of F[x].
  2. State the theorem describing all ideals of F[x].
  3. Determine whether the following statement is true: “for all f,g∈F[x], span(f,g)=⟨f,g⟩.” Justify your answer.
  4. Is gcd(2x−2,4x2−4)=2x−2 in Q[x]? Justify your answer.
  5. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if af+bg=x−1 for some a,b∈Q[x], then gcd(f,g)=x−1.” Justify your answer.
  6. Name an algorithm that computes gcd(f,g) using only division with remainder (@thm-polynomial-division).

exr-ideals-and-gcd-b1.title: B1: gcd and Bézout Coefficients of Two Cubics
exr-ideals-and-gcd-b1.title_html: B1: gcd and Bézout Coefficients of Two Cubics
exr-ideals-and-gcd-b1.html: In Q[x], let f=x3+x2+x+1 and g=x3+x+2. Use the Euclidean algorithm to find d=gcd(f,g) and polynomials a,b∈Q[x] with d=af+bg. Hence find all complex numbers that are roots of both f and g.

exr-ideals-and-gcd-b2.title: B2: Ideal or Not?
exr-ideals-and-gcd-b2.html:
Determine which of the following subsets of R[x] are ideals. For each ideal, find its monic generator. Justify your answers.

  1. S1={f∈R[x]:f(1)=f(−1)}.
  2. S2={f∈R[x]:f(0)=0 and f(1)=0}.
  3. S3={f∈R[x]:deg⁡f≥3}∪{0}.
  4. S4={f∈R[x]:f(i)=0}, where f(i) means the value at i∈C of f regarded as a complex polynomial.

exr-ideals-and-gcd-b3.title: B3: The gcd of x^m - 1 and x^n - 1
exr-ideals-and-gcd-b3.title_html: B3: The gcd of xm−1 and xn−1
exr-ideals-and-gcd-b3.html:
Let F be a field. For integers m,n≥0, not both zero, let gcd(m,n) denote the largest positive integer dividing both.

  1. For m≥n≥1, verify that xm−1=xm−n(xn−1)+(xm−n−1).
  2. Prove that gcd(xm−1,xn−1)=xgcd(m,n)−1 in F[x] for all m,n≥0 not both zero, where x0−1=0.
  3. Hence compute gcd(x12−1,x18−1).

Hint for (b): @thm-euclidean-algorithm, run on the exponents.

exr-ideals-and-gcd-c1.title: C1: Polynomials Vanishing on a Set
exr-ideals-and-gcd-c1.title_html: C1: Polynomials Vanishing on a Set
exr-ideals-and-gcd-c1.html:
Let F be a field and S⊆F non-empty. Put I(S)={f∈F[x]:f(s)=0 for all s∈S}.

  1. Prove that I(S) is an ideal of F[x].
  2. Suppose S={s1,…,sk} is finite, with the si distinct. Prove that I(S)=⟨(x−s1)⋯(x−sk)⟩.
  3. Suppose S is infinite. Prove that I(S)={0}.
  4. Deduce from (b) and @exr-division-c3 that I(Fp)=⟨xp−x⟩ for every prime p.

exr-ideals-and-gcd-c2.title: C2: A Non-Principal Ideal in Two Variables
exr-ideals-and-gcd-c2.title_html: C2: A Non-Principal Ideal in Two Variables
exr-ideals-and-gcd-c2.html:
A polynomial in two variables over F is a finite sum P=∑i,jaijxiyj with aij∈F, only finitely many non-zero; two are equal when all coefficients agree. They are added coefficient by coefficient and multiplied by expanding and collecting, and the set F[x,y] of all of them satisfies the laws of @thm-polynomial-ring-laws, which you may use. Ideals of F[x,y] and ⟨P1,…,Pk⟩ are defined exactly as in @def-ideal-polynomials, and @prp-ideal-generated holds with the same proof. For P≠0, let degy⁡P be the largest j with aij≠0 for some i, and define degx⁡P similarly.

  1. Prove that degy⁡(PQ)=degy⁡P+degy⁡Q for non-zero P,Q∈F[x,y]. By symmetry the same holds for degx.
  2. Show that ⟨x,y⟩ consists of the polynomials whose constant coefficient a00 is 0.
  3. Prove that ⟨x,y⟩≠⟨D⟩ for every D∈F[x,y].
  4. Explain precisely which step of the proof of @thm-ideals-principal has no analogue in F[x,y].

Hint for (a): write P=∑jpj(x)yj with pj∈F[x], and use @cor-polynomial-no-zero-divisors.

exr-ideals-and-gcd-c3.title: C3: gcd Times lcm
exr-ideals-and-gcd-c3.html:
Let F be a field and f,g∈F[x] monic. Put d=gcd(f,g) and write f=df1, g=dg1 with f1,g1∈F[x].

  1. Prove that gcd(f1,g1)=1.
  2. Prove that m=df1g1 is a monic common multiple of f and g that divides every common multiple of f and g.
  3. Deduce that lcm(f,g)=df1g1, and hence gcd(f,g)⋅lcm(f,g)=fg.
  4. Show by an example in Q[x] that the formula in (c) fails if f and g are not monic.

Hint for (b): use @thm-coprime-divides-product.

exr-interpolation-and-crt-a1.title: A1
exr-interpolation-and-crt-a1.html:
1. Define the Lagrange basis for distinct nodes c0,…,cn, and state the value of ℓi at cj.
  2. True or false: for four distinct nodes, the polynomial of degree at most 3 through the four points always has degree exactly 3. Justify your answer.
  3. State the Chinese Remainder Theorem for polynomials, with all hypotheses.
  4. True or false: if gcd(m1,m2,m3)=1, then every system f≡ri(modmi), i=1,2,3, has a solution. Justify your answer.
  5. What is dimR⁡R[x]/⟨x4+1⟩? Give a basis.
  6. Which functional on F[x]≤n is the i-th vector of the dual basis (@thm-dual-basis) of the Lagrange basis?

exr-interpolation-and-crt-b1.title: B1: A Lagrange interpolant
exr-interpolation-and-crt-b1.html: Let c0,c1,c2,c3=0,1,2,3. Write down the Lagrange basis for these nodes in factored form, and use it to find the p∈Q[x]≤3 with p(0)=1, p(1)=0, p(2)=1 and p(3)=10. Hence compute p(4).

exr-interpolation-and-crt-b2.title: B2: A CRT system
exr-interpolation-and-crt-b2.html: Find the polynomial f∈Q[x] of degree less than 3 with f≡2(modx−1) and f≡x(modx2+1). Hence describe all g∈Q[x] satisfying both congruences.

exr-interpolation-and-crt-b3.title: B3: The Lagrange basis sums to one
exr-interpolation-and-crt-b3.title_html: B3: The Lagrange basis sums to one
exr-interpolation-and-crt-b3.html:
Let c0,…,cn∈F be distinct with Lagrange basis (ℓ0,…,ℓn).

  1. Prove that ℓ0+ℓ1+⋯+ℓn=1.
  2. Prove more generally that ∑i=0ncikℓi=xk for k=0,1,…,n (with c0=1).
  3. For n=2 and nodes 0,1,2, verify (a) by expanding.

exr-interpolation-and-crt-c1.title: C1: Interpolation over a finite field
exr-interpolation-and-crt-c1.title_html: C1: Interpolation over a finite field
exr-interpolation-and-crt-c1.html:
Let p be a prime and F=Fp.

  1. Explain why @thm-lagrange-interpolation cannot be applied with more than p nodes.
  2. Let E:Fp[x]≤p→Fpp, E(f)=(f(0),f(1),…,f(p−1)). Prove that E is linear and surjective but not injective, and find a non-zero polynomial in kerE.
  3. Deduce that every function Fp→Fp is the polynomial function of exactly one polynomial of degree at most p−1, but of more than one polynomial of degree at most p.

exr-interpolation-and-crt-c2.title: C2: Newton’s form of the interpolant
exr-interpolation-and-crt-c2.title_html: C2: Newton’s form of the interpolant
exr-interpolation-and-crt-c2.html:
Let c0,…,cn∈F be distinct. Put N0=1 and Nk=(x−c0)(x−c1)⋯(x−ck−1) for 1≤k≤n+1.

  1. Prove that (N0,…,Nn) is a basis of F[x]≤n.
  2. Let p=∑k=0nakNk. Show that p(ci)=∑k=0iakNk(ci) and Ni(ci)≠0. Explain why the coefficients a0,a1,… of the interpolant can be found one at a time, and show that a0=y0 and a1=y1−y0c1−c0.
  3. Let pn∈F[x]≤n interpolate y0,…,yn at c0,…,cn, and let cn+1 be a further node, distinct from the others, with a value yn+1. Prove that the interpolant pn+1∈F[x]≤n+1 is pn+1=pn+yn+1−pn(cn+1)Nn+1(cn+1)Nn+1.
  4. Find the Newton form of the interpolant of @exr-interpolation-and-crt-b1, and then the interpolant after adding the point (4,0). Why is this more economical than recomputing with Lagrange’s formula?

Hint: for (c), check the values of the right-hand side at all n+2 nodes.

exr-polynomials-of-operators-a1.title: A1
exr-polynomials-of-operators-a1.html:
1. State what it means that p↦p(T) is linear and multiplicative.
  2. True or false: if p(T)q(T)=0, then p(T)=0 or q(T)=0. Justify your answer.
  3. Why does every operator on a finite-dimensional space have a non-zero annihilating polynomial? Is the same true on F[x]?
  4. True or false: if p annihilates T and p∣q, then q annihilates T. Justify your answer.
  5. State the kernel splitting lemma for (pq)(T)=0, and say where coprimality is used in its proof.
  6. True or false: for every subspace U of V and every T∈L(V), T maps U into U. Justify your answer.

exr-polynomials-of-operators-b1.title: B1: A polynomial of a 2 \times 2 matrix
exr-polynomials-of-operators-b1.title_html: B1: A polynomial of a 2×2 matrix
exr-polynomials-of-operators-b1.html:
Let A=(123−1)∈M2(Q).

  1. Compute p(A) for p=x2−7 and for q=x2+x−5.
  2. Hence show that A is invertible and find A−1 as a polynomial in A.

exr-polynomials-of-operators-b2.title: B2: An annihilating polynomial by elimination
exr-polynomials-of-operators-b2.title_html: B2: An annihilating polynomial by elimination
exr-polynomials-of-operators-b2.html:
Let C=(00210−1012)∈M3(Q).

  1. Compute C2 and C3, and show that (I3,C,C2) is linearly independent.
  2. Find a linear dependence among I3,C,C2,C3, and hence a monic polynomial p of degree 3 with p(C)=0.
  3. Hence show that C is invertible and write C−1 as a polynomial in C.

exr-polynomials-of-operators-b3.title: B3: Operators with T^3 = T
exr-polynomials-of-operators-b3.title_html: B3: Operators with T3=T
exr-polynomials-of-operators-b3.html:
Let F have characteristic not 2, and let T∈L(V) with T3=T.

  1. Use @thm-kernel-splitting with p=x and q=x2−1 to show V=kerT⊕ker(T2−idV), with projection idV−T2 onto kerT.
  2. Show that V=kerT⊕ker(T−idV)⊕ker(T+idV).
  3. Verify that the projections onto the three summands in (b) are idV−T2, 12(T2+T) and 12(T2−T), in the sense that these three operators sum to idV and each maps V into the corresponding kernel.

exr-polynomials-of-operators-c1.title: C1: Inverses are polynomials
exr-polynomials-of-operators-c1.html:
Let V be a vector space over F and T∈L(V).

  1. Suppose p(T)=0 for some p∈F[x] with p(0)≠0. Prove that T is invertible and that T−1=g(T) for some g∈F[x].
  2. Deduce that if V is finite-dimensional and T is invertible, then T−1 is a polynomial in T.
  3. Show that the monic generator m of IT, for V finite-dimensional and non-zero, satisfies m(0)≠0 if and only if T is invertible.

Hint: for (b), write a non-zero annihilating polynomial as xkp1 with p1(0)≠0.

exr-polynomials-of-operators-c2.title: C2: Splitting with k coprime factors
exr-polynomials-of-operators-c2.title_html: C2: Splitting with k coprime factors
exr-polynomials-of-operators-c2.html:
Let T∈L(V), and let p1,…,pk∈F[x] be non-zero and pairwise coprime, with k≥2. Put p=p1⋯pk and W=kerp(T).

  1. Use @thm-crt-polynomials to find e1,…,ek∈F[x] with ei≡1(modpi) and ei≡0(modpj) for j≠i. Show that p∣e1+⋯+ek−1 and that p∣piei for each i.
  2. Prove that for every w∈W, w=e1(T)w+⋯+ek(T)w with ei(T)w∈kerpi(T).
  3. Prove that W=kerp1(T)⊕⋯⊕kerpk(T), and that ei(T) is the identity on kerpi(T) and zero on kerpj(T) for j≠i.
  4. Deduce: if p(T)=0, then V=kerp1(T)⊕⋯⊕kerpk(T), and the projection onto the i-th summand along the others is the polynomial ei(T).

Hint: for the second divisibility in (a), use @lem-coprime-product (b).

exr-polynomials-of-operators-c3.title: C3: The same rotation over \nR and over \nC
exr-polynomials-of-operators-c3.title_html: C3: The same rotation over R and over C
exr-polynomials-of-operators-c3.html:
Let A=(0−110), so that A2+I2=0.

  1. Over C, apply @thm-kernel-splitting to TA on C2 with p=x−i and q=x+i. Find both kernels and write the projection onto ker(A−iI2) as a polynomial in A.
  2. Over R, show that the only subspaces of R2 that TA maps into themselves are {0} and R2. Explain why this matches the fact that x2+1 admits no factorization into coprime non-constant factors in R[x].

exr-roots-and-multiplicity-a1.title: A1
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-a1.html:
1. Define the multiplicity of c as a root of a non-zero f∈F[x]. Why is f≠0 required?
  2. True or false: if f(c)=f′(c)=0, then c has multiplicity exactly 2. Justify your answer.
  3. True or false: over every field, f′=0 implies that f is constant. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: if f∈R[x] has degree 4 and the multiplicities of its real roots add up to 4, then f splits over R. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: if f∈Q[x] is non-constant and gcd(f,f′)≠1, then f has a repeated irreducible factor. Justify your answer.
  6. Name the dual basis (@thm-dual-basis) of (1,x−c,…,(x−c)n) in R[x]≤n.

exr-roots-and-multiplicity-b1.title: B1: Multiplicities over different fields
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-b1.html:
1. Let f=x5−3x4+4x3−4x2+3x−1. Find mult1(f) in Q[x]. Hence decide whether f splits over R, and whether it splits over C.
  2. In F2[x], find the roots of g=x4+x2 and their multiplicities. Does g split over F2?

exr-roots-and-multiplicity-b2.title: B2: A gcd test
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-b2.html: Decide whether f=x4−2x2+1∈Q[x] has a repeated root, by computing gcd(f,f′) with the Euclidean algorithm. Hence factor f and give all multiplicities.

exr-roots-and-multiplicity-b3.title: B3: The multiplicity of 1
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-b3.title_html: B3: The multiplicity of 1
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-b3.html: Let n≥2 and f=xn−nx+n−1∈Q[x]. Prove that 1 is a root of f of multiplicity exactly 2.

exr-roots-and-multiplicity-c1.title: C1: Real roots of the derivative
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-c1.title_html: C1: Real roots of the derivative
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-c1.html:
Let f∈R[x] have degree n≥2 and split over R. Prove that f′ splits over R. You may use Rolle’s theorem from calculus: if a<b are real and f(a)=f(b)=0, then f′(ξ)=0 for some ξ with a<ξ<b.

Hint: count the roots of f′ with multiplicity, and compare with deg⁡f′.

exr-roots-and-multiplicity-c2.title: C2: x^p - x over \nF_p
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-c2.title_html: C2: xp−x over Fp
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-c2.html:
Let p be a prime and f=xp−x∈Fp[x].

  1. Compute f′ and deduce that f has no repeated irreducible factor.
  2. Using @exr-polynomials-c2, deduce that xp−x=∏a∈Fp(x−a).
  3. Explain why the argument of (a) gives nothing for g=xp−1. Then prove that g=(x−1)p in Fp[x].

Hint for (c): for 0<k<p, use the integer identity k(pk)=p(p−1k−1).

exr-roots-and-multiplicity-c3.title: C3: Removing repeated factors
exr-roots-and-multiplicity-c3.html:
Let F be a field and f=ap1e1⋯prer∈F[x], where a∈F∖{0}, the pi are distinct monic irreducible polynomials and ei≥1.

  1. Suppose F has characteristic 0. Prove that gcd(f,f′)=p1e1−1⋯prer−1, and deduce that f/gcd(f,f′)=ap1⋯pr.
  2. Over F2, let f=x2(x+1). Compute f/gcd(f,f′) and show that the conclusion of (a) fails.

Hint for (a): write D=p1e1−1⋯prer−1. Show D∣gcd(f,f′); for the reverse, show piei∤f′ using Euclid’s lemma.

exr-unique-factorization-a1.title: A1
exr-unique-factorization-a1.html:
1. Define what it means for p∈F[x] to be irreducible over F.
  2. State the Unique Factorization Theorem in F[x].
  3. Determine whether the following statement is true: “a polynomial in R[x] of degree at least 1 with no real root is irreducible over R.” Justify your answer.
  4. Is the constant 2 irreducible over Q? Is 2x+4?
  5. Is x2+1 irreducible over F5? Justify your answer.
  6. Name a tool that reduces the irreducibility of a cubic in Z[x] over Q to finitely many evaluations.

exr-unique-factorization-b1.title: B1: Irreducible or Not?
exr-unique-factorization-b1.html:
Determine whether each polynomial is irreducible over each of the given fields. Justify your answers.

  1. x2+2 over Q, R, F2 and F3.
  2. x3+x+1 over F2 and over F3.
  3. x3−3x−1 over Q.
  4. x4+4 over Q.
  5. x5−6x+3 over Q.

exr-unique-factorization-b2.title: B2: Factoring x^6 - 1 Over \nQ
exr-unique-factorization-b2.title_html: B2: Factoring x6−1 Over Q
exr-unique-factorization-b2.html: Factor x6−1 into monic irreducible polynomials over Q, and justify that each factor is irreducible. Hence find its factorization into monic irreducibles over F2 as well. Is it obtained by reducing the coefficients of each rational factor modulo 2? Explain why, in general, this has to be checked rather than assumed.

exr-unique-factorization-b3.title: B3: Small Irreducibles Over \nF_2
exr-unique-factorization-b3.title_html: B3: Small Irreducibles Over F2
exr-unique-factorization-b3.html:
List all irreducible polynomials over F2 of degree at most 3. Justify that your list is complete.

Hint: a polynomial over F2 has the root 0 exactly when its constant term is 0, and the root 1 exactly when its number of non-zero terms is even.

exr-unique-factorization-c1.title: C1: Infinitely Many Irreducibles
exr-unique-factorization-c1.html:
Let F be any field.

  1. Prove that there are infinitely many monic irreducible polynomials over F.
  2. Deduce that for every prime p and every N∈N, there is an irreducible polynomial over Fp of degree greater than N.
  3. Explain why (a) is immediate when F is infinite, and use @exr-unique-factorization-b3 to name an irreducible polynomial of degree 3 over F2.

Hint for (a): imitate the proof that there are infinitely many primes (@thm-infinitely-many-primes).

exr-unique-factorization-c2.title: C2: Gauss’s Lemma and Eisenstein’s Criterion
exr-unique-factorization-c2.title_html: C2: Gauss’s Lemma and Eisenstein’s Criterion
exr-unique-factorization-c2.html:
Let Z[x] be as in @thm-rational-root, and let p be a prime. For g=∑bixi∈Z[x], define its reduction modulo p as g¯=∑[bi]xi∈Fp[x], where [b] is the class of b in Fp=Z/pZ (@exm-finite-fields).

  1. Prove that g+h―=g¯+h¯ and gh―=g¯h¯ for all g,h∈Z[x], and that deg⁡g¯≤deg⁡g.
  2. Let g,h∈Z[x], and suppose p divides every coefficient of gh. Prove that p divides every coefficient of g or every coefficient of h.
  3. (Gauss’s lemma.) Let f∈Z[x], and suppose f=gh with g,h∈Q[x]. Prove that there is a non-zero λ∈Q with λg∈Z[x] and λ−1h∈Z[x].
  4. Let F be a field, c∈F non-zero, n∈N, and u,v∈F[x] with uv=cxn. Prove that u=βxs and v=γxt for some non-zero β,γ∈F and s,t∈N.
  5. Prove @thm-eisenstein-criterion.

Hint for (c): among all ways of writing kf=(αg)(βh) with α,β∈Q, αβ=k a positive integer and αg,βh∈Z[x], take k as small as possible. Hint for (e): suppose f=gh with g,h non-constant, use (c), and reduce modulo p.

lem-coprime-product.title: Coprime to Each, Coprime to the Product
lem-coprime-product.title_html: Coprime to Each, Coprime to the Product
lem-coprime-product.html:
1. Let p,q1,…,qs∈F[x]. If p is coprime to each qj, then there are a,b∈F[x] with ap+bq1⋯qs=1, and p is coprime to q1⋯qs.
  2. Let m1,…,mk∈F[x] be non-zero and pairwise coprime, that is, gcd(mi,mj)=1 whenever i≠j. If mi∣h for every i, then m1⋯mk∣h.

lem-dalembert.title: d’Alembert’s Lemma
lem-dalembert.html: Let p∈C[x] be non-constant, and let z0∈C with p(z0)≠0. Then there is z∈C with |p(z)|<|p(z0)|.

lem-euclid-step.title: Dividing Does Not Change the Ideal
lem-euclid-step.title_html: Dividing Does Not Change the Ideal
lem-euclid-step.html: Let F be a field and f,g,q,r∈F[x] with f=qg+r. Then ⟨f,g⟩=⟨g,r⟩. Consequently gcd(f,g)=gcd(g,r).

lem-irreducible-gcd.title: The gcd with an Irreducible Polynomial
lem-irreducible-gcd.title_html: The gcd with an Irreducible Polynomial
lem-irreducible-gcd.html: Let F be a field, p∈F[x] irreducible over F, and f∈F[x]. Then either p∣f or gcd(p,f)=1.

lem-minimum-modulus-attained.title: The Minimum of \lvert p \rvert Is Attained
lem-minimum-modulus-attained.title_html: The Minimum of |p| Is Attained
lem-minimum-modulus-attained.html: Let p∈C[x]. Then there is z0∈C with |p(z0)|≤|p(z)| for every z∈C.

lem-multiplicity-cofactor.title: Multiplicity via the Cofactor
lem-multiplicity-cofactor.html: Let f∈F[x] be non-zero, c∈F and m∈N. Then multc(f)=m if and only if f=(x−c)mgfor some g∈F[x] with g(c)≠0.

lem-polynomial-growth.title: Growth of a Polynomial
lem-polynomial-growth.html: Let p=anxn+⋯+a1x+a0∈C[x] with n≥1 and an≠0. Put A=|a0|+|a1|+⋯+|an−1|,R=max{1,2A|an|}. Then for every z∈C with |z|≥R, |p(z)|≥12|an||z|n≥12|an||z|. In particular, for every real M≥0, we have |p(z)|>M whenever |z|≥R and |z|>2M/|an|.

prp-coprime-criterion.title: Coprime Means 1 Is a Combination
prp-coprime-criterion.html: Let F be a field and f,g∈F[x]. Then f and g are coprime if and only if there exist a,b∈F[x] with af+bg=1.

prp-divisibility-properties.title: Rules for Divisibility
prp-divisibility-properties.html:
Let F be a field and f,g,h∈F[x].

  1. If f∣g and g∣h, then f∣h.
  2. If h∣f and h∣g, then h∣af+bg for all a,b∈F[x].
  3. If g∣f and f≠0, then deg⁡g≤deg⁡f.
  4. f∣g and g∣f if and only if f and g are associates or both are 0. In particular, if f∣g, g∣f, and f,g are both monic, then f=g.
  5. If g≠0, then g∣f if and only if the remainder of f on division by g is 0.

prp-gcd-independent-of-field.title: The gcd Is the Same Over a Larger Field
prp-gcd-independent-of-field.title_html: The gcd Is the Same Over a Larger Field
prp-gcd-independent-of-field.html: Let K be a subfield of a field L, and let f,g∈K[x]. Then the greatest common divisor of f and g computed in K[x] equals the one computed in L[x]. In particular, f and g are coprime over K if and only if they are coprime over L.

prp-ideal-generated.title: The Ideal Generated by Finitely Many Polynomials
prp-ideal-generated.title_html: The Ideal Generated by Finitely Many Polynomials
prp-ideal-generated.html: Let F be a field and f1,…,fk∈F[x], with k≥1. Then ⟨f1,…,fk⟩ is an ideal of F[x] containing f1,…,fk. Moreover, every ideal J of F[x] with f1,…,fk∈J satisfies ⟨f1,…,fk⟩⊆J.

thm-annihilating-polynomial-exists.title: Every Operator Satisfies a Polynomial
thm-annihilating-polynomial-exists.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F with dim⁡V=n, and let T∈L(V). Then there is a non-zero p∈F[x] with deg⁡p≤n2 and p(T)=0. The same holds for every A∈Mn(F).

thm-annihilator-ideal.title: The Annihilating Polynomials Form an Ideal
thm-annihilator-ideal.title_html: The Annihilating Polynomials Form an Ideal
thm-annihilator-ideal.html:
Let V be a vector space over F and T∈L(V), and let IT:={p∈F[x]:p(T)=0}.

  1. IT is an ideal of F[x].
  2. Either IT={0}, or there is a unique monic m∈F[x] with IT=⟨m⟩. In the second case, for every p∈F[x], p(T)=0⟺m∣p, and m has the least degree among the non-zero polynomials annihilating T.
  3. If V is finite-dimensional, then IT≠{0}, and deg⁡m≤(dim⁡V)2.

thm-coprime-divides-product.title: A Coprime Factor Can Be Canceled
thm-coprime-divides-product.title_html: A Coprime Factor Can Be Canceled
thm-coprime-divides-product.html: Let F be a field and p,q,r∈F[x]. If p∣qr and gcd(p,q)=1, then p∣r.

thm-crt-isomorphism.title: CRT as an Isomorphism
thm-crt-isomorphism.html: Let m1,…,mk∈F[x] be non-zero and pairwise coprime, and put m=m1⋯mk. Then Φ:F[x]/⟨m⟩→F[x]/⟨m1⟩×⋯×F[x]/⟨mk⟩,f+⟨m⟩↦(f+⟨m1⟩,…,f+⟨mk⟩), is a well-defined isomorphism of vector spaces.

thm-crt-polynomials.title: Chinese Remainder Theorem for Polynomials
thm-crt-polynomials.html:
Let m1,…,mk∈F[x] be non-zero and pairwise coprime, and put m=m1⋯mk. For all r1,…,rk∈F[x]:

  1. there is f∈F[x] with f≡ri(modmi) for every i;
  2. if f and g both satisfy (a), then f≡g(modm);
  3. there is exactly one such f with deg⁡f<deg⁡m.

thm-dimension-polynomial-quotient.title: Dimension of F[x]/\langle m \rangle
thm-dimension-polynomial-quotient.title_html: Dimension of F[x]/⟨m⟩
thm-dimension-polynomial-quotient.html: Let m∈F[x] be non-zero of degree d. Then F[x]/⟨m⟩ is finite-dimensional with dim⁡F[x]/⟨m⟩=deg⁡m=d. If d≥1, the cosets (1+⟨m⟩,x+⟨m⟩,…,xd−1+⟨m⟩) form a basis.

thm-eisenstein-criterion.title: Eisenstein’s Criterion
thm-eisenstein-criterion.html:
Let f=anxn+an−1xn−1+⋯+a0∈Z[x] with n≥1, and let p be a prime such that

  1. p∤an;
  2. p∣ai for every i=0,1,…,n−1;
  3. p2∤a0.

Then f is irreducible over Q.

thm-euclid-lemma-polynomials.title: Euclid’s Lemma for Polynomials
thm-euclid-lemma-polynomials.html: Let F be a field and p∈F[x] irreducible over F. If q,r∈F[x] and p∣qr, then p∣q or p∣r.

thm-euclidean-algorithm.title: Euclidean Algorithm
thm-euclidean-algorithm.html:
Let F be a field and f,g∈F[x] with g≠0. Put r−1=f and r0=g. As long as rk≠0, divide rk−1 by rk (@thm-polynomial-division): rk−1=qk+1rk+rk+1,deg⁡rk+1<deg⁡rk. Then:

  1. the process stops: there is an index n with 0≤n≤deg⁡g such that rn≠0 and rn+1=0;
  2. if c is the leading coefficient of this last non-zero remainder rn, then gcd(f,g)=c−1rn.

thm-evaluation-homomorphism.title: Evaluation at an Operator
thm-evaluation-homomorphism.html:
Let V be a vector space over F and T∈L(V). Then the map F[x]→L(V),p↦p(T), has the following properties.

  1. It is linear: (cp+q)(T)=cp(T)+q(T) for all p,q∈F[x] and c∈F.
  2. It is multiplicative and sends 1 to idV: (pq)(T)=p(T)q(T) and 1(T)=idV.
  3. Its image {p(T):p∈F[x]} is a subspace of L(V), closed under composition, in which any two operators commute.
  4. If S∈L(V) commutes with T, then S commutes with p(T) for every p∈F[x].

thm-formal-derivative-rules.title: Rules for the Formal Derivative
thm-formal-derivative-rules.html:
Let F be a field, f,g∈F[x], a,b,c∈F and m≥1 an integer. Then:

  1. (af+bg)′=af′+bg′, and a′=0 for the constant polynomial a;
  2. (fg)′=f′g+fg′ (product rule);
  3. (gm)′=mgm−1g′; in particular ((x−c)m)′=m(x−c)m−1.

thm-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra.title: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
thm-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra.html: Every non-constant polynomial p∈C[x] has a root in C.

thm-gcd-properties.title: Characterization of the gcd
thm-gcd-properties.html:
Let F be a field, f,g∈F[x], and d=gcd(f,g).

  1. d∣f and d∣g.
  2. If h∈F[x] satisfies h∣f and h∣g, then h∣d.
  3. If f,g are not both zero, then d is the only monic polynomial with properties (a) and (b).

thm-ideals-principal.title: Every Ideal of F\lbrack x\rbrack Is Principal
thm-ideals-principal.title_html: Every Ideal of F[x] Is Principal
thm-ideals-principal.html: Let F be a field and I an ideal of F[x]. If I≠{0}, there is exactly one monic polynomial d with I=⟨d⟩. Moreover, d is the unique monic polynomial of least degree in I.

thm-irreducible-deg-2-3.title: Irreducibility in Degree 2 and 3
thm-irreducible-deg-2-3.html:
Let F be a field and p∈F[x].

  1. p has a factor of degree 1 in F[x] if and only if p has a root in F. In particular, if deg⁡p≥2 and p has a root in F, then p is reducible over F.
  2. If deg⁡p∈{2,3}, then p is irreducible over F if and only if p has no root in F.

thm-kernel-image-of-polynomial-invariant.title: T Preserves Kernels and Images of Polynomials in T
thm-kernel-image-of-polynomial-invariant.title_html: T Preserves Kernels and Images of Polynomials in T
thm-kernel-image-of-polynomial-invariant.html:
1. Let R,S∈L(V) with SR=RS. Then Sv∈kerR for every v∈kerR, and Sw∈imR for every w∈imR.
  2. In particular, for T∈L(V) and p,q∈F[x], the operator q(T) maps kerp(T) into kerp(T) and imp(T) into imp(T). Taking q=x: T maps kerp(T) and imp(T) into themselves.

thm-kernel-splitting.title: Kernel Splitting Lemma
thm-kernel-splitting.html:
Let V be a vector space over F, let T∈L(V), and let p,q∈F[x] be coprime. Choose a,b∈F[x] with ap+bq=1 (@cor-bezout-polynomials), and put W=ker(pq)(T),E1=b(T)q(T),E2=a(T)p(T). Then:

  1. W=kerp(T)⊕kerq(T);
  2. E1+E2=idV, and for every w∈W, the splitting of w in (a) is w=E1w+E2w,E1w∈kerp(T),E2w∈kerq(T); so E1 maps W into W and acts on W as the projection onto kerp(T) along kerq(T), and E2 acts on W as the projection onto kerq(T) along kerp(T);
  3. in particular, if (pq)(T)=0, then V=kerp(T)⊕kerq(T), and the projections of V onto the two summands along each other are the polynomials (bq)(T) and (ap)(T) in T.

thm-lagrange-interpolation.title: Lagrange Interpolation
thm-lagrange-interpolation.html:
Let n∈N, let c0,…,cn∈F be distinct, and let (ℓ0,…,ℓn) be the Lagrange basis for these nodes.

  1. ℓi(cj)=δij for all i,j∈{0,…,n}.
  2. (ℓ0,…,ℓn) is a basis of F[x]≤n, and every p∈F[x]≤n satisfies p=∑i=0np(ci)ℓi.
  3. For all y0,…,yn∈F, the unique p∈F[x]≤n with p(ci)=yi for every i is p=∑i=0nyiℓi.

thm-multiplicity-of-product.title: Multiplicity of a Product
thm-multiplicity-of-product.html: Let f,g∈F[x] be non-zero and c∈F. Then multc(fg)=multc(f)+multc(g).

thm-polynomial-division.title: Polynomial Division with Remainder
thm-polynomial-division.html: Let F be a field, and let f,g∈F[x] with g≠0. Then there exist unique polynomials q,r∈F[x] such that f=qg+randdeg⁡r<deg⁡g.

thm-polynomial-function-determines-polyn.title: Values Determine a Polynomial
thm-polynomial-function-determines-polyn.html:
Let F be a field and p,q∈F[x].

  1. Let n∈N with deg⁡p≤n and deg⁡q≤n. If p(c)=q(c) for at least n+1 distinct elements c∈F, then p=q.
  2. If F is infinite and p(c)=q(c) for every c∈F, then p=q.

thm-polynomial-taylor.title: Taylor Expansion of a Polynomial
thm-polynomial-taylor.html:
Let F be a field, n∈N and c∈F.

  1. The list Bc=(1,x−c,(x−c)2,…,(x−c)n) is a basis of F[x]≤n.
  2. Suppose F has characteristic 0, or characteristic p>n. For k=0,…,n define φk:F[x]≤n→F by φk(f)=f(k)(c)k!. Then (φ0,…,φn) is the dual basis of Bc, and every f∈F[x]≤n satisfies f=∑k=0nf(k)(c)k!(x−c)k.

thm-rational-root.title: Rational Root Theorem
thm-rational-root.html: Let f=anxn+an−1xn−1+⋯+a0∈Z[x] with n≥1 and an≠0. If u/v∈Q is in lowest terms and f(u/v)=0, then u∣a0 and v∣an.

thm-real-roots-conjugate-pairs.title: Conjugate Roots Have Equal Multiplicity
thm-real-roots-conjugate-pairs.html: Let f∈R[x] be non-zero, regarded as an element of C[x], and let z∈C. Then f(z―)=f(z)―. In particular z is a root of f if and only if z― is, and multz―(f)=multz(f).

thm-remainder-theorem.title: Remainder Theorem and Factor Theorem
thm-remainder-theorem.html:
Let F be a field, f∈F[x] and c∈F.

  1. The remainder of f on division by x−c is the constant f(c).
  2. c is a root of f if and only if x−c∣f.

thm-repeated-root-derivative.title: Repeated Root Test
thm-repeated-root-derivative.html:
Let F be a field, f∈F[x] non-zero and c∈F.

  1. c is a multiple root of f if and only if f(c)=0 and f′(c)=0.
  2. Suppose multc(f)=m≥1 and m⋅1≠0 in F (this holds automatically if F has characteristic 0). Then f′≠0 and multc(f′)=m−1.

thm-roots-with-multiplicity.title: Roots Counted with Multiplicity
thm-roots-with-multiplicity.html: Let F be a field and f∈F[x] non-zero. Let c1,…,ck be the distinct roots of f in F, with multiplicities m1,…,mk. Then f=(x−c1)m1⋯(x−ck)mkg for some g∈F[x] with no root in F. Consequently m1+⋯+mk≤deg⁡f, with equality if and only if f splits over F.

thm-unique-factorization-polynomials.title: Unique Factorization in F\lbrack x\rbrack
thm-unique-factorization-polynomials.title_html: Unique Factorization in F[x]
thm-unique-factorization-polynomials.html:
Let F be a field and f∈F[x] non-constant.

  1. Existence. There are a non-zero constant c∈F, an integer k≥1, and monic polynomials p1,…,pk∈F[x], each irreducible over F, with f=cp1p2⋯pk.
  2. Uniqueness. If also f=c′q1q2⋯ql with c′∈F non-zero, l≥1, and q1,…,ql monic and irreducible over F, then c=c′, k=l, and after renumbering the qj we have pi=qi for every i.

In both factorizations, the constant is the leading coefficient of f.
